Erigon used to stream, I know that for sure, I assume it still can if it's direct. What I'm trying to understand is how big can be an output from debug_traceBlock, and I got lucky with that block as it is really big. With block gas limit increase, this will get even bigger, there some interesting suggestions to reduce the trace size : https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/762#discussion_r3043703653 https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/762#discussion_r3059867903 Erigon may have disabled streaming by default, cuz they used to break and return invalid JSON when there was a panic/crash/whatever We have acknowledged that the method isn't perfect and there are issues, but these are issues that have existed for like 10 years at this point. If we have to go completely back to the drawing board and re-architect the opcode tracer then once again perfection will be the enemy of progress, and for the 87th time the effort to standardization of the method will fail. The gas limit isn't even the problem, there are individual transactions, like the one linked in the geth issue that are also ridiculous https://etherscan.io/tx/0xd80a10106f2a8fb76cf6db6b9f7a64f08257b4952c94c888e1ac41ceb80733c9 fwiw I just sat down to check, Erigon does stream `< Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and does not OOM and is documented via the flag `--rpc.streaming.disable` haha it didn't OOM but it did produce invalid JSON: `jq: parse error: Unfinished JSON term at EOF at line 1, column -1578612014` hmmm maybe it did OOM odd <@745384946310578317> for awareness i got about 2.5gb output then memory spikes and oom I don't have a Nethermind archive node to test with Reth does not support streaming afaik geth doesn't support streaming either, unless you debug to a file? But geth doesn't OOM, it times out with `execution timeout` at least lol > But geth doesn't OOM, it times out with execution timeout at least lol That's interesting, we had to introduce a new timeout defaulted to 10 minutes to address these cases. I could try exporting the geth trace to a file via `debug_standardTraceBlockToFile` would that help with your comparison? I could host it on Google Drive or something lol If you actually need it, and it's not just a curiosity 😆 I think the output of that method is slightly different though so it would be hard to compare anyway I wanted to check if it is not an error from besu side, at least on size output, so I think it will help if you can dump it to disk. Comparing two files of 600 GiB seems not simple so I need to think about it. Maybe first step is just if you can dump it to file Actually, I think I can get a trace from Nethermind from the guys at QuickNode, lemme see if they'll do it lol do you just wanna know its output size? yes, exactly Ok I'll get back to you as soon as I get a number Nethermind also has an execution timeout, but if we specify timeout value in the request, we also hit their default 20s json-rpc timeout. The QuickNode team will test again later today with a node with a longer timeout 😂 Nethermind also cannot generate the trace, it also will OOM an internal process, the node itself doesn't OOM but it'll return: ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":"System.OutOfMemoryException: Exception of type 'System.OutOfMemoryException' was thrown.\n at Nethermind.Core.Extensions.SpanExtensions.ToHexViaLookup( ... ``` i've opened this: https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/20738
